pr_body:
In case `/var/lib/kubelet` is a symlink, `losetup -j <device in/var/lib/kubelet>` will show the device paths with symlinks fully evaluated.

Fix the routine that parses  `losetup -j` and expand symlinks in the path that we want to find there.

/kind bug

issue_context.title: Block devices are not torn down when /var/lib/kubelet is symlink
issue_context.body:
**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
1. Make /var/lib/kubelet a symlink
    ```
    mkdir -p /tmp/data/kubelet
    ln -s  /tmp/data/kubelet /var/lib/kubelet
    ```

1. Run  kubelet
    ```
    hack/local-up-cluster.sh
    ```

1. Create a block PVC + a pod that uses it.
1. Delete the pod.

-> The pod is `Terminating` forever. In kubelet logs:
```
W1126 13:11:25.728798    4415 volume_path_handler_linux.go:61] couldn't find loopback device which takes file descriptor lock. Skip detaching device. device path: "/var/lib/kubelet/plugins/kubernetes.io/aws-ebs/volumeDevices/aws:/us-east-
1d/vol-0b1729094ca87a001/7e04362d-39c9-4417-874a-618d5c9a9924"
```

The reason is that `losetup -j /var/lib/kubelet/plugins/kubernetes.io/aws-ebs/volumeDevices/aws:/us-east-1d/vol-0b1729094ca87a001/7e04362d-39c9-4417-874a-618d5c9a9924` shows:
```
/dev/loop0: [0005]:53278 (/tmp/data/kubelet/plugins/kubernetes.io/aws-ebs/volumeDevices/aws:/us-east-1d/vol-0b1729094ca87a001/7e04362d-39c9-4417-874a-618d5c9a9924)
```

kubelet can't find `/var/lib/kubelet/plugins...` there, because losetup shows real path `/tmp/data/kubelet/plugins...`.

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): 1.18

/sig storage
/priority important-soon

review_comments: should we instead call `losetup` on expanded path, so as if behaviour of losetup changes in future - we don't break anything?
I think evaluating paths before calling losetup is not useful. But I see your point, I added check for both `realPath` and original `path`, just in case.

> I think evaluating paths before calling losetup is not useful.

Can you explain why is it not useful? Do you foresee any breakage? From very afar it sounds like it is better to pass expanded path to losetup and scan for only one path rather than two (both real and symlink).

The initial concern was that losetup can change in the future and it may not expand symlinks in `losetup -j` output. So if it lists symlinks instead of evaluating them, we should check for the unevaluated path too.
